content.title: About
content.content: Pre‑gelatinized sorghum flour is made from whole sorghum grains that have been heat‑treated to partially gelatinize the starch. This makes the flour instantly soluble, improves viscosity, and allows use without additional cooking. The flour is light‑yellow, neutral in flavor, and suitable for gluten‑free recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sorghum is one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown in Africa and Asia for over 5,000 years.
Sorghum flour is naturally gluten‑free, making it safe for people with celiac disease.
Pre‑gelatinization reduces cooking time and enhances the texture of finished dishes.
Sorghum is rich in iron and phosphorus, providing valuable minerals.
Compared with corn flour, sorghum retains more of its natural nutrients after processing.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Sorghum provides a notable amount of iron, which is essential for hemoglobin formation and energy production.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The dietary fiber in sorghum flour promotes healthy bowel function and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Pre‑gelatinized sorghum releases glucose more slowly, beneficial for blood‑sugar management.

items.title: Source of magnesium
items.content: Magnesium from sorghum supports muscle and nerve function and participates in metabolic processes.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phenolic compounds in sorghum help combat free radicals and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Although sorghum is considered low‑allergen, some individuals may react to grain proteins.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Sorghum contains modest levels of oxalates, which could contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible persons.

items.title: Additive awareness
items.content: When buying pre‑gelatinized flour, check the ingredient list for anti‑caking agents or other additives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use sorghum flour in gluten‑free breads, pancakes, muffins, sauces, and soups. Its pre‑gelatinized nature allows easy dissolution in cold liquids, making it ideal for smoothies and protein shakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation.
